title: Governor of Minnesota

context.text: Open seat: incumbent DFL Gov. Tim Walz announced in January 2026 that he would not seek a third term.
U.S. Sen. Amy Klobuchar launched her campaign on January 29, 2026 and won the DFL primary on August 11 with about 90% of the vote, ahead of Kobey Layne (about 6%) and five other candidates.
House Speaker Lisa Demuth won the Republican primary with about 43% of the vote, ahead of Mike Lindell (about 33%) and Kendall Qualls (about 21%) among seven candidates.

Green Party nominee Steven Young is the only other candidate on the November ballot for governor: the county sample ballot lists exactly three tickets (Klobuchar/Schierer, Demuth/Wilson and Young/Kirby), as do MPR News and Sahan Journal.

candidates.name: Amy Klobuchar
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Ben Schierer, former mayor of Fergus Falls. Won the Aug. 11 DFL primary with about 90% of the vote.

priorities.text: Lower costs: health care and prescription drugs, housing, child care and utility bills, including building more homes and expanding child care access.
Make government accountable and root out fraud, with modern technology and easier permitting.
Workforce: doubling apprenticeships and workforce training and raising academic achievement with evidence-based curriculum and tutoring.
Also lists crime and public safety, rural and agricultural economy, and conservation and outdoor recreation among her priorities.

record.text: Voted no on the Laken Riley Act (S. 5), which passed the Senate 64–35.
Voted no on H.R. 1 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act) in the Senate, which passed 50–50 with the Vice President breaking the tie.

candidates.name: Lisa Demuth
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Ryan Wilson, attorney and 2022 state auditor nominee. Won the Aug. 11 Republican primary with about 43% of the vote.

priorities.text: Affordability: $150 million in property tax cuts, a $99 maximum car tab fee, income tax cuts for working families by reducing the lowest two brackets, ending automatic gas tax increases and eliminating the state tax on Social Security benefits.
Fraud prevention: replacing agency commissioners, adding forensic accountants and unannounced site visits, and prison sentences and asset seizure for people who steal from welfare programs.
priorities.quote: If you steal welfare from our state, you're going to prison – with no exceptions.

priorities.text: Education: opting Minnesota into the federal $1,700 education tax credit, school safety funding for every school, and a focus on reading and math fundamentals.
Public safety: increased penalties for repeat violent crime and assaulting an officer, support for law enforcement recruitment and retention, and clearing camps on state land.

positions.summary: Would opt Minnesota into the federal education tax credit, which her plan says unlocks scholarships for public, charter and private school students.
Her public safety plan calls for funding for violent crime enforcement teams, law enforcement recruitment and retention incentives, and training reimbursement.
Her agenda calls for lowering the state's business tax rates and cutting income tax rates for working families rather than raising taxes.

record.text: Voted yes on S.F. 856 creating an Office of the Inspector General, which passed the House 127–5.
Voted no on a motion to suspend the rules to bring H.F. 5140 (regulating semiautomatic military-style assault weapons and large-capacity magazines) to a vote; the motion failed 67–67.
Voted yes on a motion to suspend the rules to bring H.F. 5084, a proposed constitutional amendment recognizing a right to life for the preborn, to a vote; the motion failed 52–71.
Voted yes on S.F. 4401 (Omnibus Cannabis bill), which passed the House 92–42.

candidates.name: Steven Young

priorities.quote: Green jobs. Save the environment, juice the economy
Unified defense against federal over reach. Neighborhood-based, state-backed defense to ensure that our neighbors aren't kidnapped.

positions.summary: His campaign site lists abolishing ICE and making Minnesota a sanctuary state among his key issues.
positions.quote: I know that the governor can't technically abolish ICE, but I can make their lives miserable while they're in our state.

statements.quote: We have a world to save! We cannot afford to put off the many climate change mitigation and preparation that we need to do.
statements.context: On his campaign website, under Green Jobs

candidates.researchNotes: Sources are his campaign website and the KAXE candidate questionnaire. Other sources (a conservative news site and a candidate-survey site) report positions on single-payer health care and guns, but they were not used as a basis. No direct statement found on abortion, taxes or school choice.

researchNotes: Running mates are listed in each candidate's ballotNote rather than as separate entries. Ballotpedia and the Minnesota Secretary of State candidate site were blocked (bot check); the three-ticket slate was confirmed on the printed Freeborn County General Election sample ballot (Klobuchar and Schierer, Demuth and Wilson, Steven Young and Jane Kirby; write-in line only otherwise), and MPR News and Sahan Journal agree (Wikipedia spells the first name 'Steve'; Mike Newcome withdrew in March 2026 per Wikipedia and is not on the ballot). Primary-result percentages come from Wikipedia's results tables. Klobuchar's housing plan and priorities pages are cited for her one listed position; her other plan pages were not read. Demuth's votes are Minnesota House roll calls from the official House vote pages (bill descriptions from the House vote snapshot); several are procedural motions and are described as such. Federal key votes for Klobuchar are expected to be added by script.
